newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends sharply higher, soyoil firmer.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends sharply higher, soyoil firmer.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended sharply higher on Tuesday, led by old crop on talk of export business and on short covering in the July, traders said.
Soyoil also posted strong gains in reaction to strength in soybeans and soymeal.

U.S. exporters could not confirm rumors that China had bought a cargo of U.S. soymeal but commercials were aggressive buyers of old crop soymeal on Monday which traders said lent credence to the rumors. Commercials were again strong buyers of old crop on Wednesday, led by Cargill Inc.
The lack of deliveries also lifted the July.
Some trade sources had anticipated deliveries after cash soymeal premiums slipped. But cash sources on Tuesday quoted soymeal offers for Chicago at $5.00 over CBOT July.

New crop soy products were also higher but traders cited spread alignment rather than fundamental strength. They noted soybean crop conditions improved last week, boosting arguments for a bumper crop. Some analysts have put new crop soybean output at a record 2.8 to 2.9 billion bushels.
Soymeal ended $9.00 to $1.70 per ton higher with July up $9.00 at $251.50. Soyoil closed 0.31 to 0.24 cent per lb higher with July up 0.31 at 22.15.

On the day, funds bought at least 1,600 lots soymeal, led by Smith Barney who bought 1,000 August and 100 December. Rand Financial bought 500 December and R.J. O'Brien bought 400 August, pit sources said.
Commercials were buyers of soyoil. Cargill Inc bought 800 August and 200 December while Produce Grain bought 300 August and 200 July, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 30,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 25,222 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 13,000 lots, against Monday's 14,112 lots.
